claims.text: An 11-year-old girl from a rural community was referred to a pediatric dentistry clinic for comprehensive dental care. A previous hematologist had diagnosed symptomatic mild hemophilia A with 46% factor VIII activity and normal von Willebrand factor; she was under on-demand treatment and her father had moderate hemophilia A. A previous extraction by a general dentist had caused excessive, uncontrolled bleeding.

claims.text: At the second visit she received 1,000 IU of factor VIII one hour before the appointment, then extractions of #55, #53, #65, #75 and a mesiodens under topical benzocaine for mobile primary teeth and limited lidocaine with epinephrine infiltration for #65 and the mesiodens, with hemostasis by sterile gauze. She was observed for 30 minutes and discharged with written instructions to avoid NSAIDs and use acetaminophen; no postoperative bleeding or complications occurred. Postoperative photographs were taken at 30 minutes and one month.
